title: CAP theorem
summary: The document introduces the CAP theorem in database theory, stating that distributed data stores can provide at most two of three guarantees: consistency, availability, and partition tolerance. It explains how network partitions force a choice between consistency and availability, and discusses the historical context, evolution, and related concepts like the PACELC theorem.

title: HTTP/2
summary: HTTP/2 is a major revision of the HTTP network protocol designed to reduce latency and improve web page loading speeds. Derived from Google's experimental SPDY protocol and standardized by the IETF in 2015, it introduces features such as request multiplexing, header compression, and server push over a single TCP connection. While it retains the high-level semantics of HTTP/1.1, its reliance on a single TCP connection can lead to head-of-line blocking issues, eventually motivating the development of HTTP/3.
tags: computer science, distributed systems
